title: Open diagonal of an unramified algebraic space over a scheme
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme, $T$ an $S$-scheme [def-pc-scheme], and $A$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $f:A\to T$ be unramified, meaning that for every representable etale scheme chart $V\to A$ the composite $V\to T$ is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Then the diagonal
$$\Delta_f:A\longrightarrow A\times_T A$$
is a representable open immersion. Explicitly, for every $S$-scheme $Z$ and every morphism $b:Z\to A\times_T A$, the sheaf fibre product $Z\times_{b,A\times_T A,\Delta_f}A$ is represented by an open subscheme of $Z$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. Here the fibre products are fibre products of the functors of points, evaluated on each test scheme.

source.place: Tag 05W1 (lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism), part (1), with target a scheme; unramifiedness is tested on etale scheme charts as in Tag 03ZK (lemma-unramified-local).

proof.text: Put $P=A\times_T A$, with projections $\pi_1,\pi_2$. Fix an arbitrary scheme $b:Z\to P$ and write $a_i=\pi_i b$. The pullback $W=Z\times_{P,\Delta_f}A$ is the equality functor: its points over $Z$ are precisely those maps $z:C\to Z$ for which $a_1z=a_2z$, and the accompanying point of $A(C)$ is then uniquely $a_1z$. It is a scheme: it is also the pullback of the representable diagonal $A\to A\times_S A$ along $(a_1,a_2)$, using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. This identification is on every test scheme, not just on points over fields. The projection $h:W\to Z$ is a monomorphism, since there is at most one accompanying point of $A(C)$ for any $z$. Choose a representable surjective etale atlas $q:U\to A$ with $U$ a scheme, again by [def-trf-algebraic-space].

source.place: Tag 05W1 (lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism), first sentence: representable monomorphism, here proved directly from the diagonal clause of Tag 025Y (spaces.tex, definition-algebraic-space).

proof.text: The hypothesis applies to the chart $q:U\to A$: $f q:U\to T$ is an unramified morphism of schemes. By [def-weil-unramified-morphism], its diagonal $d:U\to U\times_T U$ is an open immersion. The scheme fibre product exists by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] therefore makes $d$ etale. This is exactly the scheme-diagonal input in the proof of Tag 05W1, taking the target chart to be $T\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}T$.

source.place: Tag 05W1 (lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism), part (1), paragraph beginning Assume f is unramified; scheme input morphisms.tex Tag 02GE (lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism) and Tag 02GP (lemma-open-immersion-etale).

proof.text: The induced map $v=q\times_T q:U\times_T U\to P$ is representable etale, as follows directly on test schemes. Given $c:C\to P$, form the schemes $C_i=C\times_{\pi_i c,A,q}U$. By the representable-etale clause of [def-trf-algebraic-space], $C_i\to C$ is etale. On a scheme over $C$, a pair of lifts to $U$ has equal composites to $T$, because $c$ is a point of $P$. Consequently $C\times_P(U\times_T U)$ is represented by $C_1\times_C C_2$, with exactly those pairs as its points. Existence and this universal description use [def-pc-fibre-product]. The projection to $C_1$ is etale by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits], applied to $C_2\to C$; composing with $C_1\to C$ is etale by part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. This proves the assertion about $v$ on every test scheme.

source.place: Tag 05W1 (lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism), displayed diagram with V=T, middle vertical arrow; scheme base change and composition are morphisms.tex Tags 02GO and 02GN.

proof.text: For the fixed $b:Z\to P$, let $C=Z\times_P(U\times_T U)$, a scheme etale over $Z$ by Step 3, and set $E=C\times_{U\times_T U,d}U$. This is a scheme by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Its projection to $C$ is etale by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] and the etaleness of $d$ in Step 2. Part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] makes $E\to Z$ etale. The defining pairs identify $E$ with $Z\times_{P,\Delta_f q}U$: a point is $(z,u)$ with $b(z)=(q(u),q(u))$. Thus this argument explicitly checks the needed base change of the composite, rather than inferring a property of a sheaf map from its underlying set.

source.place: Tag 05W1 (lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism), left square, with V=T; pull back its composite to the arbitrary scheme Z, using morphisms.tex Tags 02GO and 02GN.

proof.text: There is a canonical identification $E\cong W\times_A U$, where $W\to A$ is $a_1h=a_2h$. Indeed on a test scheme over $Z$, a point of the right side is $(z,x,u)$ with $a_1z=x=a_2z$ and $q(u)=x$; forgetting $x$ gives exactly $(z,u)$ with $b(z)=(q(u),q(u))$, the description of $E$ in Step 4. Inserting $x=q(u)$ is the inverse, and both operations commute with every restriction map. The projection $p:E\to W$ is therefore a surjective etale morphism of schemes by the representable-surjective-etale meaning of the atlas $q$ in [def-trf-algebraic-space].

source.place: Tag 05W1 (lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism), surjective etale left vertical arrow, pulled back to W; atlas base-change convention is spaces.tex Tag 025Y (definition-algebraic-space).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-etale-descent-through-source-cover] with its schemes $(T,X,Y)=(Z,W,E)$ and its arrows $(h,p)$ equal to those above. Step 5 supplies surjectivity and etaleness of $p$, and Step 4 supplies etaleness of $hp:E\to Z$. Hence $h:W\to Z$ is etale. The cited statement imposes no quasi-compactness on the cover and no separation, finite-type or Noetherian assumption on the schemes, so it applies to this arbitrary test scheme $Z$.

source.place: Tag 05W1 (lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism), etale-locality conclusion in part (1); implemented after scheme base change by descent.tex Tag 036W (lemma-etale-etale-local-source), singleton source cover.

proof.text: By [def-weil-etale-morphism], $h$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. It is a monomorphism by Step 1, so [lem-pe-flat-lfp-monomorphism-open] applies and shows that $h$ is an open immersion. Equivalently its source $W$ is isomorphic over $Z$ to an open subscheme of $Z$, by [def-weil-open-immersion]. Since $Z$ and $b$ were arbitrary, this proves the representable-open-immersion assertion for $\Delta_f$ and the explicit equality-locus clause, with the full scheme structures throughout.

source.place: Tag 025G (theorem-etale-radicial-open), (3) implies (1), the final input to spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 05W1 (1).
